issues.description: Sequential per-image getIamPolicy calls turn N+1 listing into latency-dominated O(N) round trips with no batching or threading.
issues.detail: The other compute resources use __threading_call__, but _get_images iterates images serially within a single project loop. For projects with many custom images this is asymptotically fine but practically slow: total time is N * RTT. Either use the batch HTTP API or parallelize per image as is done for regions/zones.

issues.description: IAM-policy exception handler dereferences error.__traceback__.tb_lineno, which can be None and raise a secondary AttributeError.
issues.detail: When an exception is constructed but not raised (or re-raised after traceback is cleared) __traceback__ is None and tb_lineno does not exist. The test fixture even injects a synthetic Exception via side_effect; depending on path that traceback may be unstable. Use logger.exception or guard the attribute access.

issues.description: Loop invariant for publicly_shared detection is stated only implicitly; the early break is correct but unexplained, and role is ignored.
issues.detail: The invariant should read: after processing bindings[0..i], publicly_shared is true iff some processed binding lists allAuthenticatedUsers as a member. The code does not check the role, so any binding (even an irrelevant custom role) flips the flag. That may be intentional, but the literate comment should say so explicitly.

issues.description: Directory name and CHANGELOG entry disagree with the metadata CheckID convention used elsewhere.
issues.detail: PR description and code use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, but the human-readable title says publicly_shared. Minor, but a careful reader scanning the changelog versus the directory tree will stumble. Pick one form and use it everywhere including the check class docstring.

issues.description: Image model omits the role and members payload, foreclosing future checks without a service refactor.
issues.detail: Storing only a boolean publicly_shared throws away the IAM bindings already fetched. A literate data-structure choice would keep the bindings (or at least the offending role+members) so a sibling check like image_iam_overly_permissive can reuse the same getIamPolicy round trip. Cheap to add now, expensive to retrofit.

issues.description: test_compute_no_images asserts len(result) == 0 but the no-images contract is not documented in the check.
issues.detail: The check silently returns an empty list when there are no custom images. That is defensible, but a reader cannot tell from the docstring whether absence-of-images should produce an INFO finding or nothing. Add one sentence to the class docstring stating the empty-input behavior.

review.summary: The check is small, correct in the common case, and well-tested at the unit level — RIGOROUS on intent, UNDER-AUDITED on the data-fetch path. The main rigor gap is in compute_service._get_images: serial getIamPolicy calls per image (ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW), a fragile tb_lineno access inside the exception logger, and an unstated loop invariant that ignores the IAM role. The Image model is also a WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE candidate: discarding bindings forces the next image-IAM check to redo the same round trip. The check file itself is clear; a brief literate note about empty-input behavior and a CheckID/title consistency pass would finish it.
